Shared input data and file schemas:
- The preloaded arrays are independent synthetic examples, not arrays loaded from the supplied annotation files. times has shape (5,); ref_events and est_events each have shape (4,). These represent event/frame times in seconds.
- ref_intervals and est_intervals each have shape (4, 2), with start and end time columns. ref_labels and est_labels are separate lists of four chord-label strings corresponding to those interval examples.
- ref_freqs and est_freqs each have shape (5,) and contain frequency values in Hz, including zero values for unvoiced frames. ref_sources and est_sources are small synthetic numeric arrays of shape (2, 5), not recorded audio tracks.
- beat_reference_file and beat_estimate_file are String paths to existing read-only text inputs. Each noncomment data row contains one beat timestamp in seconds. beat_estimate_file also begins with a comment line whose first character is #. Neither file contains event-label or interval columns.
- chord_reference_file is a String path to an existing read-only text input with three columns: interval start, interval end, and a chord label. The start/end columns are numeric time values; the third column is text.
- melody_reference_file is a String path to an existing read-only text input with two numeric columns: time in seconds and frequency in Hz.
- output_dir is the writable directory for newly created files, separate from these input files.
These descriptions identify the supplied data; they do not select a reader API or specify an expected evaluation score.
